Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the post-incident note on the outage this morning. Our ops team recorded a degradation window from 02:21 UTC to 07:05 UTC (roughly 4 hours 44 minutes) that impacted our production inference requests. We received the brief summary but need formal confirmation on whether this qualifies under the SLA for a service credit and, if so, what the calculation looks like (percentage credit / dollar value, and how it will appear on our next invoice).

Can you confirm:
- Whether StormBridge is eligible for a credit for the Aug 19 incident
- The exact hours used for calculation and the resulting credit percentage/dollar amount
- Proposed timing/mechanism for issuance (one-time invoice credit vs applied to next billing cycle)

I've attached our internal outage traces and the window we observed (stormbridge-outage-logs-0819.zip). Please let me know if you need anything else to validate. Contracts is looped for visibility.

Appreciate a quick confirmation — this is on our finance side calendar for August close.

Thanks,
Alex Monroe
Head of Platform Reliability
StormBridge

I've attached our working spreadsheet; using the SLA terms in their contract (99.9% monthly uptime target), the calculation yields a one-time credit equal to 30% of August service charges for the impacted service tier, which translates to an estimated $18,400 credit.

Notes / asks:
- That $18,400 is the preliminary net credit after caps (per contract); I flagged that we should apply a one-time invoice credit rather than a refund.
- We need approval to issue the credit and to send their contracts team the acceptance doc for signature.
- If you want, we can propose applying the credit on their Sep invoice to simplify accounting.

Attachments included: sla-calculation-sheet-0819.xlsx (working), redwood-postmortem-2026-08-19.pdf (draft).

Can I get a sign-off to proceed?

Thanks,
Soojin
